post:

headline: Star Wars unreleased Jabba prototype reveals surprises
post:
A fascinating look at a 2004 Hasbro Star Wars Saga Collection prototype shows what could have been for the famous crime lord. Unlike the final release that only featured Jabba and his pipe, this unreleased set included a massive, detailed stone throne and a Princess Leia figure in her iconic golden bikini. Cost and changing times in 2004 likely led to trimming the set down, and the prototype currently sits at a $525 bid price.

Would you have wanted this complete set in your collection? 

#StarWars #ActionFigures #Collecting
original_title: This Unreleased Star Wars Jabba the Hutt Set Includes Something Fans Never Got in the Final Version

headline: New Marvel era: Spider-Man leads the Avengers
post:
According to Screen Rant, the Marvel Universe is launching a major new era following "Avengers: Armageddon". With the United Nations initiating a global ban on superpowers after Red Hulk's actions, a brand-new roster of Earth's Mightiest Heroes is assembling. Interestingly, Peter Parker's Spider-Man is set to lead this new team, while also dealing with the undoing of his infamous "One More Day" deal with Mephisto.

Meanwhile, other key heroes are facing massive changes. David Colton has transformed into Miracleman with near-godlike abilities, leaving Wolverine to act as his mentor. At the same time, Captain Marvel is operating at just 10% of her former power levels after absorbing a massive blast, and she is joined on the new roster by Daredevil.

Tony Stark remains absent after being kidnapped and tortured by the Knomads. Before his disappearance, Iron Man used technology to view a dark future where Spider-Man seemingly dies at the hands of Mephisto. 

Which hero's new status quo are you most excited to follow?

#MarvelComics #Avengers #SpiderMan
original_title: 13 Most Important Characters In Marvel’s Brand-New Avengers Era

post:

headline: Alan Burnett's Batman Pilot Began on Super Friends
post:
Before the legendary Fleischer Studios-inspired aesthetic of "Batman: The Animated Series" hit our screens, the Dark Knight's journey nearly started somewhere else entirely. According to /Film, a 1980s pilot written by Alan Burnett for a darker "Batman" series eventually became an episode of "The Super Powers Team: Galactic Guardians" titled "The Fear." 

While working on "Super Friends," Burnett wanted a cartoon that would honor the darker spirit of the comics. However, Hanna-Barbera and ABC were not ready to commit. This unique episode served as a beta test, featuring the very first depiction of Batman's origin outside of the comics, with Adam West voicing the Caped Crusader. 

It featured Bruce Wayne explaining his parents' murder to Robin and Wonder Woman, laying groundwork that later influenced the iconic 90s show. Have you ever watched this surprising piece of animation history? 🦇📺✨

#Batman #SuperFriends #DCAnimation
original_title: Batman: The Animated Series' First Pilot Was An Episode Of DC's Super Friends
